land.text: French Gabon, a territory of French Equatorial Africa since 1910, fully independent on 17 August 1960; Cliopatria carries the land in its French Fifth Republic row for 1958-1960

predecessors.note: 'In 1910, Gabon became a territory of French Equatorial Africa,' a federation that lasted until 1958 (Gabon page); the federation's own dossier is french-africa.

capitals.name: Libreville
capitals.note: 'Libreville is the capital and largest city.' The page does not date the seat.

correction.text: Gabon in its independence year: the Cliopatria 1961 shape unchanged, from 17 August 1960

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Gabon shape begins in 1961; the page gives 'on 17 August 1960 it became fully independent'. In 1960 Cliopatria still draws the land inside French Fifth Republic (1,030 of 1,032 cells).
0.265 M km2 against the infobox's 267,668 km2 (ratio 0.99). The page records no boundary change and is silent on the Equatorial Guinea frontier (Mbanie, Corisco Bay).
Same outline as 1961 at 0.265 M km2.

ledger.note: 17 August 1960: Gabon becomes independent from France. 'On 17 August 1960 it became fully independent'; infobox 'Independence Granted: 17 August 1960'.

certainty.note: Judgment: the frontier is the French colonial line with Cameroon, Equatorial Guinea and the Republic of the Congo; the Gabon page is silent on boundary instruments and on the Mbanie dispute, so this is not a source.

sources.title: Gabon
sources.note: Independence 17 August 1960, area 267,668 km2, Libreville, French Equatorial Africa 1910-1958, the 1964 coup. Silent on boundary disputes and on Biafra.

notes: Budget: 1 page; the page records no territorial event after independence. Not settled: the Gabon-Equatorial Guinea frontier (Mbanie and Corisco Bay; page silent). Gabon recognised Biafra in May 1968 (Nigerian Civil War page, not the Gabon page). Cliopatria's 1960 land sits in the French Fifth Republic row; Spanish Guinea (francoist-spain, 1961-1972) and Equatorial Guinea (1969-) are the seed neighbours with Cameroon and the Republic of the Congo.
